newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rank buys Tom Cobleigh pub chain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rank buys Tom Cobleigh pub chain.

text.p: British leisure and hotel company Rank Organisation Plc picked up the Tom Cobleigh chain of pubs on Tuesday, paying about two million pounds each.
Tom Cobleigh, owners of 44 managed pubs in Yorkshire and the Midlands operating under the motto "Unspoilt Pubs for Nice People", is centred on the growing trend for eating out.

Rank's agreed cash offer for Tom Cobleigh at 240 pence per share, values the company at 95.6 million pounds ($148.9 million). About 62 percent of Tom Cobleigh shareholders have already accepted the offer.
In an interview, Rank chief executive Andrew Teare told Reuters the pace of new Tom Cobleigh pub openings would now increase. Some 16 new bars should be opened this year.
Food sales in recent openings of Tom Cobleigh pubs have reached on average about 50 percent of total revenues.
In the leisure sector, spending on eating out is expected to grow strongly, at some eight percent every year over the next few years.
Teare said Rank expects a fast underlying profit stream from the purchase. "There is an underlying velocity in the profit streams," he said.
Rank expects the deal to have a neutral impact on earnings in the first full financial year and enhance earnings thereafter.
Teare said Rank would also benefit from synergies between the two companies, particularly in purchases of spirits and other alcoholic drink, where Rank is a major buyer.
He said the deal would also give Rank the chance to offer eating-out facilitiies in its leisure complexes. "The one thing we don't have is an eating-out business."

Rank's leisure and entertainment complexes, which include the Odeon cinema chain and Mecca bingo halls, currently rely on leasing out space to restaurant chains but the Tom Cobleigh purchase means it can run its own food outlets, said Teare.
"We can make substantial inroads to capture those eating-out revenues," he said. "It is a big add-on to our existing strategy."

The senior management team at Tom Cobleigh, founded in December 1991 and listed on the London stock exchange in November 1995, will stay on at Rank to develop the business under the umbrella of Rank's Recreation Division.
Rank was widely touted as a likely buyer of Tom Cobleigh after the pub chain acknowledged earlier this month it was in talks with potential suitors.
Analysts and financiers said Rank's bid had pipped an earlier offer from Yates Brothers Wine Lodges.
But Rank shares fell eight on the news to 433p as analysts doubted whether the name Tom Cobleigh would appeal country wide.
Tom Cobleigh shares were 1-1/2p higher at 235p. ($1=.6420 Pound)
